text: One morning Dupin, wearing a pair of green glasses, called on the Minister at his house and found him yawning lazily, pretending to be bored. <break time="0.8s" /> Complaining of weak eyes, Dupin used the glasses to hide his eyes while he carefully looked around the room as they talked. <break time="0.8s" /> Hanging from the fireplace by a dirty blue ribbon was a card rack, in which lay a letter, soiled and torn nearly in two. <break time="0.8s" /> It had a large black seal and was addressed to the Minister himself, so it looked nothing like the letter the Prefect had described. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet such a dirty letter did not suit the tidy Minister, and its worn edges showed it had been turned inside out like a glove. <break time="0.8s" /> Returning the next morning for the snuff box he had purposely left, Dupin was talking with the Minister when a loud shot rang out below the window. <break time="0.8s" /> As screams followed, the Minister rushed to look outside, and Dupin quickly took the letter, putting in its place a copy he had made at home. <break time="0.8s" /> The gun, which held no bullet, was fired by a man whom Dupin had paid, and he was soon let go as a madman. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside the copy, Dupin had written a line from a French play, so that the Minister would one day know who had beaten him.
